# Discarded Code

## bigrams
```{r surprisal, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
bnc_size = 96928173 # total frequencies from the prepared file (bnc whole) without punctuation

article <- article %>% 
  mutate(
    word = frequency,
    previous_word = lag(frequency),
    conditional_prob = 0,
    bigram_surprisal = log(1 / (word / bnc_size)) + log(1 / conditional_prob))
```

## valence
```{r categorical_valence}
# Turn into categorical
positive = 0.1
negative = -0.1

article <- article %>%
  mutate(AAPz_cat = case_when(
    AAPz > positive ~ "Positive",
    AAPz < negative ~ "Negative",
    TRUE ~ "Neutral"), .after = AAPz)
```

```{r}
article %>%
    group_by(AAPz_cat, lang) %>%
    summarise(val = median(dur), .groups = "drop") %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = AAPz_cat, values_from = val)
```

```{r}
article %>%
    group_by(AAPz_cat, lang) %>%
    summarise(val = median(dur), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = AAPz_cat, y = val, color = lang, group = lang)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  #facet_wrap(~lang) +
  labs(x = "Valency", y = "Median Duration", color = "Language") +
  theme_minimal()
```
**Important:** This doesn't say much about the reading times with respect to valence because other variables (such as word length) need to be considered as well.

### Language Group
#### Duration 
```{r mean_lang}
article %>% group_by(lang) %>% 
  summarize(mean_duration = round(mean(dur)), 
            median_duration = median(dur), 
            standard_deviation = round(sd(dur)))
```


## Explorations
```{r baayen_p49}
native.lm = lm(median_L1L2  ~ AAPz, native)
nonnative.lm = lm(median_L1L2  ~ AAPz, nonnative)

plot(RQ3_df$AAPz, RQ3_df$median_L1L2, xlab = "AAPz", ylab = "Duration", typ = "n") +
  #points(native$AAPz, native$median_L1L2, pch = "1", col="darkgrey") +
  lines(lowess(native$AAPz, native$median_L1L2), col="darkgrey") +
  abline(coef(native.lm), col= "darkgrey", lty=2) +
  #points(nonnative$AAPz, nonnative$median_L1L2, pch = "2") +
  lines(lowess(nonnative$AAPz, nonnative$median_L1L2))  +
  abline(coef(nonnative.lm), lty=2) 

#summary(native.lm)$coef
#summary(nonnative.lm)$coef
```

## Linear Mixed-Models
Comment: Would need ANOVA to see which model is more significant
```{r}
summary(lmer(dur ~ word_length + log_freq + punctuation + AAPz + I(AAPz^2) + is_stopword + log_freq:(AAPz + I(AAPz^2)) + punctuation:(AAPz + I(AAPz^2))
             + (1 | token) + (1 | lang / participant), article))
```

### Participant-level variables
```{r median_participants, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
median_part <- article %>% group_by(lang, textnr, tokenindex, token) %>% 
  reframe(median_lang, word_length, frequency, punctuation, AAPz, 
          mean_exposure = round(mean(exposure_EN)), 
          mean_cft = round(mean(cft20)), 
          mean_lextale = round(mean(lextale)), 
          mean_motiv = round(mean(motiv)), 
          mean_start = round(mean(start_learning))) %>%
  distinct()
```
- Do the variables *exposure_EN + cft20 + lextale + motiv + start_learning* need to be medians between language groups?
- - Doesn't make much sense to include them then.
- why is *ee* mean_start *NA*? There are some missing values, these participants will be excluded.
